newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African bank governor encouraged by trade trends.
newsitem.headline: S.African bank governor encouraged by trade trends.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Thursday that the effects of the rand's depreciation were beginning to show, with the trade balance reflecting sizeable improvement on a three-month moving average.

Financial markets cheered the dramatic turnaround in South Africa's trade account in July, which helped yields on the bond market sharply lower on Thursday. But the data drew scant applause from economists who said the indicator was unreliable.
But Stals, speaking on Business Tonight, said he was encouraged by the trend that was beginning to emerge and did not share economists' concerns.
"I think the trade statistics can change a lot from one month to the next and one should not make too much about the monthly movements in both imports and exports," he said.

"But we, the Reserve Bank, would normally look at something like a three-month moving average, and looking at a three-month moving average the trade balance improved quite a lot over the last two months.
"So, we feel that the effects of the depreciation of the rand are beginning to show up in the trade statistics," the central bank's governor said.

According to South African Revenue Service (SARS) data, the country recorded a trade surplus of 2.58 billion rand in July, up from a 27.6 million rand deficit in June and more than three times economists' most optimistic forecast of a 800 million rand surplus.
South Africa's volatile currency has fallen about 20 percent from around 3.65 to the dollar since February. The rand ended at 4.5080/5130 on Thursday.
